transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

That pattern, running about 10 minutes, stopping, then working again once it's been left, is a common sign of the dryer overheating and its safety cut-out tripping. Once it cools, the cut-out resets and it starts again. On a vented dryer, the usual root cause is that the hot, damp air can't escape fast enough. 1. Restricted airflow. This could be a fluff-packed lint filter, or a vent hose that's kinked, squashed, too long or furred up with lint.
2. 3. Less often, the blower fan not shifting enough air. 1. Lint filter. Pull out the filter in the door opening and clear all the fluff. Also wipe out any lint around the slot it sits in. If it was thick with fluff, that alone can cause exactly this.
2. Vent hose. Take it off the back of the dryer and look along its whole length. It should be as short and straight as possible, with no sharp bends or flattened sections, and clear inside. Hoses hung out of a window often get pinched by the window frame or sag and droop, which lets lint and moisture collect, so check that spot especially. Shake or clear out any lint, and refit the hose so it isn't trapped.
3. Load. A very heavy, overpacked load makes overheating more likely. Try a normal half to two-thirds full load.
4. Test run. Run a normal programme and stay nearby. You should feel a strong, steady flow of warm air. Only a weak puff points to a blockage still in the hose or inside the machine, or a fan problem. If it now runs right through, it was airflow and you're sorted. Just clean the filter every load. If it still cuts out with a clean filter, a clear, straight hose and good airflow at the outlet, that points to the thermostat or thermal cut-out, or the fan. That's the point to look at parts or an engineer, because fitting a new cut-out without fixing poor airflow just means it trips again. One safety point: if you ever notice a burning or scorched-lint smell, smoke, or the casing getting very hot, stop using it and unplug it at the wall. Lint build-up near the heater is a fire risk. ok checked the hose, its all squashed behind the dryer where i pushed it back and theres fluff in the folds. also the cabinet gets really hot before it stops. no burning smell tho

That squashed hose is very likely your culprit. When the hose is crushed, the hot, damp air can't get out. The heat builds up inside, which is why the cabinet gets really hot. The thermal cut-out then trips to protect the dryer, and it resets once it cools. Fluff collecting in the folds makes the blockage worse each time. It's good there's no burning smell, but this is exactly the situation to sort out properly. 1. Unplug the dryer and let it cool. Take the hose off, then straighten it and shake or clear out all the fluff from the folds. If it's been flattened so badly it won't spring back into a round tube, or it's split, a new hose is cheap and worth fitting.
2. Clean the lint filter in the door opening, and wipe out the fluff in the slot it sits in.
3. Refit the hose so it has room behind the dryer. Leave a gap so it isn't crushed against the wall, and keep the route as short and straight as you can to the window. Make sure the window isn't pinching it either.
4. Run a normal-sized load and stay nearby. You should feel a strong, steady flow of warm air out of the window end. If it now runs right through, the hose was the cause. Just keep the filter cleaned every load and the hose free of kinks. If it still cuts out with a clear hose, good airflow and a clean filter, the likely problem is fluff built up inside the machine's air path, or the fan not moving enough air. A faulty thermostat or cut-out is less likely. That needs the dryer opening up, so it's engineer territory. It's also worth having the inside cleaned out given how hot it has been running. If you notice a scorching smell or smoke at any point, stop and unplug it at the wall. Once you've cleared and rerouted the hose, does it run through a full programme?

ok will sort the hose and try it. its a rented flat so landlords dryer, do i need to tell them if hose is knackered?

Yes, it's worth telling them. Your tenancy agreement may have specific terms, so check that too. 1. Tell them in writing, by email or text, so there's a record. Say it has been cutting out after about 10 minutes and the cabinet was getting very hot. Mention that the hose was found squashed with fluff in the folds.
2. If the hose won't spring back into a round tube or is split, ask whether they'd like to replace it or are happy for you to. Vent hoses are cheap and just push or clip on. Many landlords will simply say go ahead and knock it off the rent or reimburse you. Get that agreed before you spend anything.
3. Be aware that a hose crushed by pushing the dryer back against the wall could be seen as day-to-day use rather than wear and tear. Given how little a hose costs, it's usually easiest just to agree it between you.
4. If it still cuts out after the hose is sorted, that's firmly the landlord's job. It would point to fluff inside the machine or a fan problem, which needs an engineer to open it up. Given how hot it has been running, an internal clean-out is sensible anyway. In the meantime, keep the lint filter cleaned every load. Stop and unplug it if you ever get a scorching smell or smoke. Let me know how the test run goes once the hose is straightened and rerouted.

ok thanks, will fix the hose and run it again then let you know how it goes

Sounds like a plan. The squashed hose is the most likely cause, so there's a good chance this sorts it. 1. Feel the window end of the hose once it's warmed up. A strong, steady flow of warm air is what you want.
2. Put your hand on the cabinet partway through. It'll be warm, but it shouldn't get as hot as before. - If it runs right through, the hose was the problem.
That's one for the landlord's engineer. If you get any scorching smell or smoke, stop it and unplug it at the wall. Let me know whether it gets through a full programme.
